sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org (Simon J. Greenhill, ed.), Kumukio lexicon: 52 items, all from McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 (The Trans-New Guinea Phylum, Pacific Linguistics B-16).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only (suli 'arm', kizap 'ear', nembelam 'tongue', paŋgat 'sun'..); transcriptions carry no stress marks. McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 itself (held) names Kumukio only in its language list and has no stress/accent passage.

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar. 2018. Comparative Morphology of the Huon Peninsula Languages (Papua New Guinea). PhD dissertation, Universität zu Köln. viii+331 pp. (KUPS 9757)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology chapter and no synchronic stress statement for any language. p.7 (pdf p.15): 'None of the three languages of this [Dallman] family has been the object of an in-depth study. For Kinalaknga and Kumukio, the only data available comes from McElhanon's surveys.' p.58: Dallman data 'comes from McElhanon's survey of 1968'. Only diachronic asides, p.125 (pdf p.133): '*u.. was not lowered in Borong, Somba, Kinalaknga and Kumukio, presumably because the suffix *-utup carried no primary stress' and 'the nominal number suffixes.. are unstressed'.
